_comment: The missions (SPEC.md §12 M27, ROADMAP.md Phase 2): the game is an engine plus a mission. Each entry is printed on the contents page, in this order. `status` is `playable`, `draft` or `coming`; a coming mission is printed but stamped NEXT YEAR'S ANNUAL and cannot be chosen, so it needs only `id`, `title`, `place`, `page` and `blurb`. A draft one (M28) is printed and stamped as a coming one, but `?mission=<id>` plays it, so it can be tried on the live site before it is announced; it needs everything a playable one does. A playable one names its `map` and `roster` files, and a `rules` and `enemies` patch deep-merged over data/rules.json and data/enemies.json before the difficulty's (the same merge difficulty.json uses; a key must already exist, except a new objective kind under `objectives` or a new enemy type under `types`). `win` is one of the fixed win conditions in src/missions.js, never a code branch for one mission. `briefing` opens the orders; `tagline` runs along the foot of the title card; `levels` (M28, optional) is the mission's own part of each difficulty level, keyed by the level's id in data/difficulty.json: a `rules` and `enemies` patch merged after the level's own, and a `summary` printed before the level's; what a level does to this mission's targets lives here, what it does in every mission lives in difficulty.json. `words` are the mission's own phrases the rules' text needs (the cut line's; the diversion's name, card and log line, M31: France's RAF diversion is the airfield's jeep raid; `cleanOrders`, M32c, optional, the operator's: the orders' line about the clean-run bonus, in the mission's words since its condition is the mission's: all night in France, only until the first bang on the airfield); `diversionSound` (M31, optional) is the sound.js cue for the diversion, `diversion` when left out; `dialogue` (M28) replaces any of the men's lines for this mission, keyed by his roster id, over the roster file's; `titleCard` is its painted title card (ART-ASSETS.md §7), France's until the file is there (M31), and `panel` (M31c, optional, any status) is its small painting beside its line on the contents page (ART-ASSETS.md §7); `titleCardLettered` (M31, optional, true when left out) says whether BURN BY DAWN is painted into it, or code must set it; `portraits` (M29b, optional) is a folder of the mission's own portraits, named as in assets/portraits, each tried before the usual one; `enemyChips` (M43, optional) is a folder of the mission's own enemy chips, named as in assets/enemies, each tried before the usual one (the aqueduct's Italians); `dropCueColour` (M58e, optional, art only) names the PALETTE colour PICK A DROP DIRECTION and the rings round the runs are drawn in, leader blue when left out (green on the frost, where blue was hard to read); `ground` (M58d, optional, art only) names the theme.js PALETTE colour the land is printed in, bare paper when left out (meadow for the green country, frost for snow, the deeper frost for winter slopes; the airfield's sand is the ochre over paper); `counterColour` (M31d, optional, art only) names the theme.js PALETTE colour our men's counters are printed in, army green when left out (the airfield's burnt orange, the operator's: green on the desert sat too close to the garrison's chits); `endSounds` are the sound.js cues for the back page; `music` (M48j, optional) is its track over the orders and the drop, a file in assets/audio named in sound.js MUSIC_TRACKS, the title music when left out (the course's); `ratings` (M32, optional) are the back page's score bands for a mission accomplished, lowest first, each a `from` score and a `label` (src/missions.js ratingOf). `?mission=<id>` in the address picks one, and `default` is the one when none is asked for.

missions._flag: M48g: a word or two printed by its line on the contents page, in the red pen. The course is where a new player starts.
missions.title: The Practice Ground
missions.blurb: The paratrooper training course, one lesson at a time.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE TRAINING BRIDGE · NOBODY GETS HURT
missions._lessons: MISSION-TRAINING.md (SPEC.md §15), M47: a mission that names a lessons file is a course. Its orders are the course's list, each lesson sets up its own men and umpires on the map, and the lesson engine (src/lessons.js) lets only what a step asks for do anything. Playable since M48g, with all seventeen lessons.
missions._rules: An exercise (data/rules.json `mission.exercise`) is never settled: nobody withdraws and there is no back page. And it has no dawn: the night is long enough that no lesson meets it. M48c: its charges take the time pencils, as the airfield's and the aqueduct's do, 2 to 4 turns (short, so no lesson ends many turns waiting for a bang).
missions._pictures: M48g. Its garrison is umpires: `enemyKit` names the drawn kit (src/render/theme.js: a service cap and a white armband), worn until a painted chip is in the `enemyChips` folder (ART-PROMPTS.md Priority 24), type by type.
missions.briefing: Today six men train on the practice ground at the paratrooper school.

missions.title: The Rail Bridge
missions.blurb: Six men drop in darkness to blow the rail line that supplies the coast. Get them out by dawn.

dakota.caption: TWENTY MINUTES TO THE DROP ZONE.

landing.caption: 0140 HOURS. SIX MEN DOWN IN THE DARK.

success.caption: THE BRIDGE IS DOWN, AND NO TRAIN COULD CROSS FOR A MONTH.

missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE BRIDGE · OUT BY DAWN
missions._rules: M38b: `turnLimit` 16 (the operator's, after a turn at 15; 20 until M38: with the train at 10 the night had five turns of slack; the bot wins as often with dawn at 15, hurrying as it nears, and the Fuel Dump becomes the thing there is rarely time for). M34: France's other patch is its goods train (data/rules.json `train`): on the Rail Bridge in the enemy phase of turn 10 (M37, the operator's: waiting for it at 17 was dull; 14 at first, then 17 from M34b, when waiting for it cost nothing), seen coming on from the west edge three turns before; the bridge down on turn 16, 17 or 18 pays 5 (the operator's: within a turn of it, score only, scenery). Everything else is the files as they are.
missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop behind enemy lines.

hard.summary: Blowing a target calls up reinforcements to guard the way out: two squads for the Rail Bridge, one for the Fuel Dump, and none once the Telephone Exchange is down.

words.cleanOrders: Getting in and out with as little enemy attention as possible earns a special bonus!

missions._ratings: M32: the back page's verdict on a mission accomplished, as score bands, lowest first (the first from 0). Set against the bot's winning scores on Normal (tools/balance-bot.mjs with SCORES=1): the bridge alone with most men out lands in the middle two; the top wants the bonus targets or a spotless night. M38b: the top from 40 (was 43), the operator's: with dawn at 16 there is rarely time for the Fuel Dump, and the greedy bot's best quarter of wins score 39 to 42. M34: 28/36/43 (were 24/30/36), for the goods train's 5 and the Fuel Dump's fifth point: the bridge alone wins 24–33, with the train 33–39, with the train and both bonus targets 42–45. Placeholder copy for the operator to reword.

missions.title: The Airfield
missions.blurb: Paratroopers raid aircraft on an Axis landing ground, on a mission to blow them sky high.

dakota.caption: RED LIGHT ON. CHECK YOUR NEIGHBOUR'S KIT.

landing.caption: A COLD, STILL DESERT NIGHT. THE STUKAS ARE UP AHEAD.

success.caption: BY DAWN THE STUKAS BURNED, AND THE MEN HAD MADE THEIR ESCAPE.

missions.tagline: SIX MEN · EIGHT AIRCRAFT · OUT BY DAWN
missions._rules: SPEC.md §13. Lewes bombs are small, so the scouts carry one each as well as the sappers (M29b, the operator's: with none, and two a sapper, the scouts had nothing to do here); still five in the stick with Nunn's. The win pays 10 on top of each aircraft's own 2, since no target here is worth the bridge's 10 on its own. M32: the garrison is Alarmed by the end of every raid here, so the clean run asks only that it was below Alert when the first bang went (and no jeep raid), and the jeep raid is urged only for men in contact, never for the Alarmed garrison. Three new objective kinds; their numbers are Normal's, first guesses for M30's balance.
missions._enemies: The perimeter car (SPEC.md §13): fast, so it reaches a noise first; it can be suppressed but never killed or knifed.

hard.summary: Seven aircraft need destroying: with your five bombs, the bowser and bomb store will both have to be blown.

missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop on an enemy airstrip in the desert.

missions.title: The Aqueduct
missions.blurb: A stone aqueduct in the mountains that takes every charge you carry. Exfil via a boat on the coast that will not wait.

dakota.caption: OVER THE MOUNTAINS, READY TO DROP. COLD AS ICE IN HERE.

landing.caption: SOUTHERN ITALY, FEBRUARY 1941. SNOW ON THE HILLS, CHARGES STASHED IN THEIR CANISTERS.

success.caption: THE AQUEDUCT WAS NO MORE, AND THE BOAT PULLED AWAY INTO THE DARKNESS.

missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE AQUEDUCT · THE BOAT WILL NOT WAIT
missions._rules: MISSION-AQUEDUCT.md (SPEC.md §14). Balanced at M42 (DECISIONS.md): the default timer is the longest, 6 (it was 4: a first charge on a short timer left the others no time to be set to the same turn, and one bang is the alert budget); the boat in on 15 and gone with 17 stands, measured; on Hard it stays two turns. Its two rules: `canisters` (the men jump with none; three canisters of two) and `exfil.opensTurn` (the boat is in on 15, gone at dawn, 18). A sapper has room for two charges, so the sappers and Nunn carry five at full pace. Time pencils as on the airfield. The patrols set out on turn 2. The aqueduct calls one squad down the road when it goes; the road bridge down stops the reserve and the squads (the exchange's payoff in France).
missions._enemies: M41b, the operator's: with men all round it, a reserve squad that could not be killed read as a fault. Here it can be, and one more comes down the road for it (rules reserve.replacements).

easy.summary: The aqueduct takes three charges, and no squad comes down the road when it's blasted.

hard.summary: The aqueduct takes all six charges, so none can be spared for the Road Bridge. With the Road Bridge still standing, two squads come down the road when the aqueduct is blasted. The boat only waits two turns, not three.

missions.briefing: Tonight six men are to drop into the mountains of southern Italy.

onLand: I can see the aqueduct from here.
Lovely place. Shame there's work to be done.

I'm fine. Get to the aqueduct.

missions._pictures: M43. Its own pictures, each a slot that falls back until the operator's painting is in the folder (ART-PROMPTS.md Priorities 19 to 21): `enemyChips`, the garrison's chips, Italian here, tried type by type before assets/enemies (the German ones); `portraits`, the six in winter kit, tried man by man before assets/portraits; `titleCard`, its own painting, France's until the file is there.
missions._ratings: M42, set against the bot's winning scores on Normal (SCORES=1): the naive bot's middle half is 26 to 31 (North 23 to 29), the tidy bot's 22 to 28 with no kills, and a stick that takes the Road Bridge too scores 32 to 35, its best quarter 35 and over. The job with every man out unseen, the Road Bridge and a clean run is 35 before kills.

missions.title: The Heavy Water Plant
missions.blurb: A heavy water plant across a frozen gorge. Get in, blow the cells and get out without a shot fired.
missions.tagline: SIX MEN · ONE STATION · NOT A SHOT FIRED
missions._rules: MISSION-GUNNERSIDE.md (SPEC.md §16). A draft (M58): every number is the spec's starting point, for M59 to measure. A 20-turn night. Tracks in the snow on (3 turns, alert +1, once an enemy phase at most). The shot: gunfire +4 and heard across the whole board, the first shot of the night asked first (confirmShot), and the clean run NOT A SHOT FIRED (cleanNoShot) pays 5. A sapper has room for two and the men jump with them, no canisters. Time pencils as on the aqueduct. The patrols set out on turn 2. A body found calls a squad to where it lay, three at most. The cell hall calls one squad up the road when it goes; the telephone line down stops the reserve and every squad (the exchange's payoff in France).

easy.summary: The cell hall takes two charges, and no squad comes up the road when it goes.

hard.summary: The cell hall takes four charges, so only one can be spared for the telephone line. With the line still up, two squads come up the road when the hall goes.
